statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail eases to 17% because the 13:30 UTC cash open printed orderly rather than as the continuation the previous cycle flagged: QQQ opened at 706.86 inside a 706.73-707.11 band, NQ trades near 29,076 at -0.17%, the 28,927.50 session low remains fully retraced, VIX is 16.20 below its 16.34 previous close and the 2Y, 10Y and 30Y are all modestly lower. Stress eases to 66% but stays high on crude near six-week highs and an active US-Iran military exchange.
recommendation: Mapped policy state is EA_ON for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD, reflecting observed two-way price discovery at the US cash open rather than an improvement in the macro backdrop. Tail remains below the block threshold for most of the next 24 hours; forecast Tail crosses it only inside the narrow 20:00-22:00 UTC window covering the Broadcom results and management call, with single-hour watch-band checkpoints at the 18:00 UTC Beige Book and the 12:30 UTC Thursday claims block. headline: Nasdaq-100 opens flat and orderly as VIX slips to 16.20, the curve eases and crude fades from six-week highs
body:
The US cash session opened at 13:30 UTC without the continuation structure the previous cycle treated as the main near-term risk. QQQ printed 706.86 at the open, down 0.11%, inside an initial 706.73-707.11 band, while NQ futures traded 29,075.25 to 29,076.00 across two independent quotes at 13:19 UTC, down 49.50 to 50.25 points or 0.17% from the 29,125.50 previous close. The day range stands at 28,927.50 to 29,170.00 on Yahoo Finance and 28,927.25 to 29,138.75 on Investing.com, leaving price in the upper half of the range and the session low fully retraced for a second consecutive hour. A marginal low that holds, followed by an opening auction that neither gaps nor extends, is the opposite of the repeated-extension-after-failed-retracement structure that defines the pathological path, and it is the primary reason Tail steps down from 18% to 17%.

Cross-asset evidence points the same way. VIX trades 16.20, down 0.14 or 0.86%, below its 16.34 previous close and well under the 16.82 session high, with the day low at 15.94. The Treasury curve is modestly lower across every tenor: 2Y 4.39% down 2.2bp, 5Y 4.55%, 10Y 4.79% down 0.8bp after touching 4.814% earlier in the session, and 30Y 5.26% down 1.8bp. Crude is retreating rather than extending, with WTI at $89.61 down 0.68% and Brent near $94.28, both off the monthly highs of $92.29 and $97.04 marked earlier in the episode. The August ADP report printed 38,000 private jobs against a 47,000 consensus, the slowest pace since January, which supports the softer front end. Yields, volatility and crude are therefore de-escalating in the same direction rather than aligning into a single amplified impulse, which is the configuration in which Tail normally stays low even while Stress remains high.

Stress eases to 66% but stays firmly in the high band, and the reasons are structural rather than intraday. The US and Iran exchanged another round of strikes overnight, with US forces targeting air defence, radar and maritime assets around the Strait of Hormuz and Iran claiming retaliation against US positions in Jordan and Bahrain. Crude remains close to six-week highs, the long end is near multi-year highs, and the Nasdaq-100 cash index closed the previous session at 29,077.22, down 1.29%, with semiconductors the weakest complex. The shared Finviz cross-asset context was collected at 09:58 UTC and is more than 90 minutes old at this assessment, so under the inherited contract it is treated as stale and this assessment rests on independently fetched primary sources.

The dominant forward risk is scheduled rather than current. Broadcom, a top-five Nasdaq-100 constituent, reports fiscal Q3 results after the 20:00 UTC close, with the management call confirmed for 2:00 p.m. Pacific Time, 21:00 UTC. The company's June 2026 report produced a 12.6% single-session decline despite beating on revenue and earnings, driven by forward AI revenue commentary on the call rather than the printed quarter, and guided Q3 AI semiconductor revenue near $16.0 billion is the stated reference point. A single-name repricing of that magnitude in a top-weight constituent, landing in a thin post-close Globex book with read-across to the wider semiconductor complex, is a credible mechanism for index-level one-way structure with a delayed second leg. That is why the danger window is placed narrowly at 20:00 to 22:00 UTC rather than across the session. Before then, Factory Orders at 14:00 UTC, EIA crude inventories at 14:30 UTC and the Beige Book at 18:00 UTC are treated as checkpoints, with only the Beige Book lifting forecast Tail into the watch band for a single hour.

lookbackSummary: The previous 24 hours began with Tail elevated at 31% around the 1 September US cash open, when the US-Iran escalation, the crude surge and the sovereign-yield selloff were being priced. Tail then decayed through the US afternoon and held a 20-25% watch band for twenty consecutive published hours, briefly touching 25% at 19:00 UTC on 1 September before easing again. The dominant mode ran as event/whipsaw through the overnight and rotated to trend-down during the European morning, then to mixed at 12:00 UTC once the session low was fully retraced. Stress stayed persistently high in a 68-77% range throughout. Three hours are unavailable because no assessment was published for them: 15:00 and 20:00 UTC on 1 September and 01:00 UTC on 2 September. Taken together the window describes a difficult, high-volatility environment in which retracements kept occurring rather than a sustained one-way trend, and this cycle's orderly cash open is consistent with that reading.
outlookSummary: The forecast holds Tail in the low band for most of the next 24 hours and lifts it above the block threshold only for the two-hour cluster from 20:00 to 22:00 UTC covering the Broadcom results and the 21:00 UTC management call, where a top-weight semiconductor constituent with a 12.6% single-session precedent can move the complex in a thin post-close book. Two single-hour watch-band checkpoints sit either side of it: the Beige Book at 18:00 UTC and the 12:00 UTC Thursday hour containing Initial Jobless Claims and the trade balance at 12:30 UTC. Stress eases gradually through the Asian session as crude and the curve are assumed to stabilise, then rebuilds into the European morning and the Thursday data block, remaining in the elevated-to-high range throughout because the crude, sovereign-yield and geopolitical backdrop is structural rather than intraday. Confidence decays with horizon from 88% to 58%, reflecting that the current reading rests on directly observed price-path evidence while later hours rest on conditional scenarios.
